config.footerNote: Original practice questions written to the AQA GCSE Religious Studies A (8062) specification, using the question structure for exams from June 2026 (1, 1, 4, 6, 12 marks). Not past-paper material. Model answers are indicative exemplars, not official AQA mark schemes; other valid answers are credited in the exam.

Beliefs.1: 1 mark (AO1). Two kinds of 1-mark item: (a) multiple choice — choose the one correct answer from A–D; (b) short response ('Give one…' / 'Name…') — one accurate, relevant point earns the mark; extra points are not needed and do not add marks.
Beliefs.4: Explain two ways (4 marks, AO1). For each of two ways: a simple explanation of a relevant, accurate point = 1 mark; a detailed (developed) explanation = 2 marks. In the Beliefs section these items usually ask how a belief influences Christians today (AO1:2 influence on individuals, communities and societies).
Beliefs.6: Explain two… and refer to sacred writings or another source of Christian belief and teaching (6 marks, AO1). First point: simple explanation 1 mark, detailed explanation 2 marks. Second point: simple 1, detailed 2. Source of authority: 2 marks for naming AND applying a relevant source (e.g. a Bible passage, creed, catechism or church teaching) to the question; 1 mark for only naming it or only applying it. Up to 6 marks in total. (From June 2026 this replaced the former 5-mark item; the question stem is unchanged.)
Beliefs.12: Evaluate (12 marks, AO2: analyse and evaluate aspects of religion and belief, including significance and influence). Levels of response, best fit. Level 4 (10–12): a well-argued response with reasoned consideration of different points of view; logical chains of reasoning leading to judgement(s) supported by accurate knowledge; religious teaching applied to the issue. Level 3 (7–9): reasoned consideration of different points of view; logical chains of reasoning drawing on relevant knowledge; clear reference to religion. Level 2 (4–6): reasoned consideration of one point of view, OR recognition of different points of view each supported by relevant reasons; maximum Level 2 if there is no reference to religion. Level 1 (1–3): a point of view with reason(s) stated in support. 0: nothing worthy of credit. Answers must follow the four bullets: refer to Christian teaching, argue for the statement, argue for a different view, and reach a justified conclusion. Up to 3 extra marks for spelling, punctuation and grammar (SPaG) are awarded on the 12-mark question in the Beliefs section: High 3 (consistent accuracy, wide range of specialist terms), Intermediate 2, Threshold 1.

Practices.1: 1 mark (AO1). Two kinds of 1-mark item: (a) multiple choice — choose the one correct answer from A–D; (b) short response ('Give one…' / 'Name…') — one accurate, relevant point earns the mark; extra points are not needed and do not add marks.
Practices.4: Explain two ways (4 marks, AO1). For each of two ways: a simple explanation of a relevant, accurate point = 1 mark; a detailed (developed) explanation = 2 marks. In the Practices section these items often ask for two different ways a practice is carried out or understood within Christianity (AO1:3 similarities and differences), or for two ways a practice influences Christians.
Practices.6: Explain two… and refer to sacred writings or another source of Christian belief and teaching (6 marks, AO1). First point: simple explanation 1 mark, detailed explanation 2 marks. Second point: simple 1, detailed 2. Source of authority: 2 marks for naming AND applying a relevant source (e.g. a Bible passage, creed, catechism or church teaching) to the question; 1 mark for only naming it or only applying it. Up to 6 marks in total. (From June 2026 this replaced the former 5-mark item; the question stem is unchanged.)
Practices.12: Evaluate (12 marks, AO2: analyse and evaluate aspects of religion and belief, including significance and influence). Levels of response, best fit. Level 4 (10–12): a well-argued response with reasoned consideration of different points of view; logical chains of reasoning leading to judgement(s) supported by accurate knowledge; religious teaching applied to the issue. Level 3 (7–9): reasoned consideration of different points of view; logical chains of reasoning drawing on relevant knowledge; clear reference to religion. Level 2 (4–6): reasoned consideration of one point of view, OR recognition of different points of view each supported by relevant reasons; maximum Level 2 if there is no reference to religion. Level 1 (1–3): a point of view with reason(s) stated in support. 0: nothing worthy of credit. Answers must follow the four bullets: refer to Christian teaching, argue for the statement, argue for a different view, and reach a justified conclusion. SPaG is not assessed on the Practices 12-mark question (it is assessed on the Beliefs 12-mark question).
